The input is copied into a heap buffer and NUL-terminated so it can be passed as a C string.
The attacker-controlled bytes are preserved verbatim in the query-name string.
The crafted name is handed to the DNS query encoder, which will parse labels and write them into an output packet buffer.
The encoder sizes its output buffer from the attacker-controlled string length before validating the detailed label structure.
A heap buffer of the computed size is allocated for the encoded DNS packet.
The function copies each label byte-by-byte into the packet buffer while interpreting dots and escapes from the attacker input.
The final packet length is derived from the write cursor after encoding the name and question fields.
